candidates.title: File:A Mandapa infront of Pampa Sarovar (02).jpg
candidates.author: iMahesh
candidates.description: The image showcases a mandapa situated in front of Pampa Sarovar, a revered water tank located in Anegundi. This mandapa serves as a significant architectural feature, often used for religious gatherings and rituals, reflecting the area's historical importance as a pilgrimage site. Pampa Sarovar is deeply embedded in local mythology, believed to be associated with the epic Ramayana, where the goddess Pampa is said to have performed penance. The mandapa's serene location, with the tranquil waters of Pampa Sarovar as a backdrop, enhances its spiritual atmosphere, inviting visitors to pause and contemplate the rich cultural narratives tied to this sacred site.

candidates.title: File:അനേഗുണ്ടിയിലെ ശിലാഫലകം.jpg
candidates.author: Kavth
candidates.description: Anegundi previously called Kishkindha is a village in the Gangavathi taluk, Koppal district in the Indian state of Karnataka,[2] It is older than Hampi situated on the northern bank of Tungabhadra River, Huchappayana matha temple (with black-stone pillars and dance sculptures), Pampa Sarovar, Aramane (a ruined palace), Ranganatha temple, Kamal Mahal, and Nava Brindavana are the major attractions Nimvapuram, a nearby village, has a mount of ash believed to be the cremated remains of monkey king Vaali. Anegundi is best visited along with Hampi, it is part of the world Heritage Site, Hampi, being developed into a world class tourism spot by engaging the locals to sensitise them to their cultural wealth and provide them a means of livelihood. Existing tanks in the village have been redesigned to store clean drinking water and proper drainage facilities developed to keep the surroundings clean and hygienic. The Kishkinda Trust is working on tourism development in Anegundi.
